To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have determined charge-independent effective interactions for the 0g_9/2- 1p_1/2 space that reproduce the energies of 47 7 levels of nuclei with Z=38 to 50 and N=47 to 50 to within a root mean square deviation of 0.15 MeV, and that these interactions are in better agreement with the data than the effective interactions determined previously.
We have developed a method to extract the matrix elements of the charge-independent effective Hamiltonian in a model space from the energies of nuclei in that model space.

we have determined the matrix elements of the charge-independent effective Hamiltonian in 0g9 /2-1p 1 /2 space by a least-square fitting of the energies of 447 levels of nuclei with Z=38 to 50, N=47 to 50.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a charge-independent effective interaction for shell-model studies of nuclei in the 0f7/2-1g9/2 space.
the development and use of a charge-dependent shell-model interaction for nuclei in the 0f7/2-1g9/2 shell.
the development of a new effective Hamiltonian in order to describe the low-lying states of nuclei in the 38≤Z,47≤N≤60 mass range.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this effective interaction is the most accurate one available at the present time for shell-model studies of nuclei in the 0f7/2-1g9/2 shell.
